ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: It is known that in the parallelogram $ABCD$, points $E$ and $F$ are respectively on sides $AB$ and $BC$, with $DE=AF$, $DE\perp AF$ at point $G$. If $\angle BAD=90^\circ$, parallelogram $ABCD$ is a square; extending $CB$ to point $H$, making $BH=AE$, determine the shape of $\triangle AHF$ and explain the reason.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}
To prove: $\triangle AHF$ is an isosceles triangle, for the following reasons:\\
From (1) we have: $\triangle ADE \cong \triangle BAF$,\\
$\therefore AE=BF$,\\
$\because BH=AE$,\\
$\therefore BF=BH$,\\
$\because$ quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore AB \perp BC$ i.e., AB bisects FH perpendicularly,\\
$\therefore AH=AF$,\\
$\therefore \boxed{\triangle AHF \text{ is an isosceles triangle}}$.

method.method_draft: Use a synthetic congruence plus perpendicular-bisector argument. From the square diagram, read that E lies on AB, F lies on BC, H is on the extension of CB beyond B, so H, B, F are collinear, and AB is perpendicular to BC. From the text, use DE = AF and BH = AE. Since ABCD is a square, AD = AB and ∠DAE = ∠ABF = 90°. Thus right triangles ADE and BAF have equal hypotenuses DE = AF and one equal leg AD = AB, so they are congruent by RHS/HL. Therefore AE = BF. Because BH = AE, we get BH = BF, so B is the midpoint of HF. Since AB ⟂ HF, line AB is the perpendicular bisector of HF. Point A lies on this perpendicular bisector, hence AH = AF. Therefore triangle AHF is isosceles.
